scope: Observed eligibility/selection diagnosis for delaying the single confirmation until both initial branches have been evaluated. Fixed set of 26 already completed episodes before TSP repetition 1 closes. Not an executed policy comparison and not a speedup prediction.
hypothesis: Compare the two independently prepared initial methods on development before spending the one confirmation. If no method reaches the existing development effect threshold, continue exploration; confirmation failure does not itself terminate exploration. Later confirmation behavior and final independent audit stay subject to a separately frozen online protocol.
interpretation: Four observed initial choices would differ when both initial methods are available: Abalone-1 candidate, KMNIST-1 candidate, TREC-0 control and TREC-1 candidate. All four original confirmations failed, but the replacement methods have no corresponding observed confirmation; success is unknown.

Four complete initial comparisons select the same method. This includes TREC-0 candidate, whose later subword neural extension was needed for its observed success; the candidate rule must not stop exploration merely because initial confirmation fails.

Fifteen early-terminal cases never executed the sibling proposal; fourteen passed final audit. Delaying confirmation would require admitting/parsing the sibling and evaluating it if format-valid instead of immediately marking it unused. The potential execution/selection/latency/success penalty cannot be inferred from missing predictions or model-generated time estimates. Static validity is recorded separately and is not runtime validity.

This is more directly related to the observed selection timing failure than adding a generic development confidence gate, but benefits and costs remain unknown. It only motivates a small future paired development test after the current frozen trial closes, not a default change or generic capability claim.
